QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_42

question.text: Risk 'Leverage Risk' in a Cat III AIF context:

answer.text: Arises because SEBI prohibits all leverage in Cat III
Arises from derivative positions and can amplify losses; SEBI permits Cat III leverage up to 2x NAV with monthly reporting and internal controls
Is limited to rupee denomination only

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs can take leverage up to 2x NAV. Leverage amplifies BOTH returns and losses, creates counterparty risk via prime brokers, and requires monthly SEBI reporting + fund-level internal controls for compliance. The Trap: A is wrong — SEBI PERMITS Cat III leverage. C/D are fabrications. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) tests zero-leverage rule; XIX-E tests 2x Cat III rule — classic split. Manager's Pro-Tip: Disclose GROSS and NET leverage separately to LPs. A market-neutral book can show 4x gross exposure but < 0.5x net — SEBI's 2x cap is on NET (fund policy usually clarifies this).
